text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government has appointed a national ad hoc committee to oversee the buying and export of rice as well as the import and sale of fertilizers.

-- A delegation from the Ministry of Defense, led by Director of the External Relations Department Colonel Vu Tan, visited the United States for the first time since diplomatic relations were established two years ago.
-- The price of electricity is likely to rise to 680 dong (5.8 U.S. cents) per kwh from 600 from April 1, Government Office Minister Lai Van Cu said.

-- The State Bank of Vietnam has issued new regulations on mortgages and guarantees for bank loans, which stipulate that land-use certificates and land-related properties may be used as mortgages only at Vietnamese banks.

-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI) has suggested that the government allow overseas Vietnamese and permanent foreign residents to set up private enterprises, limited companies and joint-stock companies in Vietnam.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet, receiving incoming Brazilian ambassador Christiano Whitaker, underlined Vietnam's will to develop relations between the two countries.

-- Vice Prime Minister Phan Van Khai received a delegation from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which is working on the next stage of enhanced structural adjustment facility (ESAF) and structural adjustment credit (SAC) programmes.
-- Thai Foreign Affairs Minister Prachuap Chaiyasan left Hanoi for Ho Chi Minh City for the second leg of a three-day visit to Vietnam.

-- A campaign against drugs will be launched on Thursday in Ho Chi Minh City, where several cases of abuse and trafficking were uncovered in recent days. Ho Chi Minh City's acting mayor, Vo Viet Thanh, said city authorities will take firm measures to eliminate drug abuse in the metropolis.
